content_source: Wikimedia Commons; manually curated; NOT Places365
selection_policy: Frozen before model evaluation. Seven distinct photographs per scene category: one pilot and six evaluation. Selected for scene relevance, different locations, composition and lighting; no stylization results used for selection. Styles are shared across pilot and evaluation, so the split does not test unseen-style generalization.
source_change: The proposed Places365 subset was not acquired. Official download page could not be reached in this session. Commons photographs replace it; the original project specification is not modified.

preprocessing.note: Images retain their downloaded aspect ratios. No local crop, filtering or model preprocessing applied. Commons uses a 1280px-wide thumbnail; Met uses its web-large JPEG. Future content preprocessing must be shared by M4/M5/M6.

content_images.title: File:Zagedan Lakes, Mountain cirque, Caucasus Mountains.jpg
content_images.label_zh: 高加索：Zagedan 山间湖
content_images.reason_zh: 山体、湖水与天空用于接口试运行。
content_images.description_html: The Zagedan lakes are of ancient glacial origin. They are surrounded by karst rock formations in a mountain cirque, which represents a typical ancient glacial landform in the Caucasus Mountains. The glacier retreated about 11,000 years ago, leaving behind the landscape we see today. Zagedan Valley with high-altitude lakes. Karachay-Cherkessia, Caucasus Mountains, Russia.

Glacial lake, rocks covered with snow, Ama Dablam (6,810 metres (22,343 ft)) and other Himalayan peaks to the south of the Great Himalayan Range in Mahalangur Himal. Nepal, Himalayas.
